context: Decision: a write appears to readers only when it completes, and a create-if-absent write fails when the name exists. The FS store gets both from a temp file and a rename or a link. Today: S3 and GCS writes appear only when they complete, but the FS backup store writes in place, so a reader can see a partial file; every backend overwrites an existing object; S3 checks a SHA-256 header, GCS a CRC32C, and the FS backup store reads the file back; no backend has a conditional write. Phase 2 needs create-if-absent for a record that a second writer must not overwrite. The title: Writes are atomic, valid, and can be exclusive.
must: exclusive|already exists|never replaces|never overwrites|if-absent|if absent|exactly one|at most one

context: Decision: the storage writer uploads a large file in parallel parts that it reads straight from ranges of the source file, and the caller only copies the file into the writer. Today: transferctl uploads huge files in parallel parts within a configured concurrency, holds no whole part in memory, resumes an upload after a restart without sending the done parts again, and reports progress; each transferctl driver runs the part logic itself. Rejected: WriteAt, which pushes every part through memory; a public WritePart. The title: Large uploads are parallel, resumable, and bounded in memory.

Decision: the browser upload by presigned chunk URLs stays a separate optional interface next to the storage interface. Today: on S3 and GCS the browser sends each chunk straight to the bucket by a signed URL; chunks go in parallel and in any order; init returns the done chunks so an upload resumes, on S3 and GCS also after a controller restart; each chunk carries a checksum; reset removes the chunks. The title: Browser uploads stay direct, parallel, and resumable.

Decision: two refreshes of one expired refresh token can race; the second gets HTTP 409 and the client retries with the new token. Rejected: a Redis single-flight lock. Today: refresh tokens are single use; the handler stores the new pair in one SQL transaction. The title: Concurrent refreshes are safe and lock-free.

Decision: `deploy --dry-run` runs the Terraform plan and prints it, and applies nothing. Today `deploy` has no preview: an operator learns what changes only after apply. The plan runs in the same Cloud Run job as apply, with the same state lock. Rejected: a separate preview service. The title: Deploy previews are complete and side-effect free.

Decision: the build moves into a pinned Docker image built by BuildKit. Today builds run on each developer laptop with the host toolchain, so the same commit can give different binaries, and a build can read files in the home directory. Rejected: Nix. The title: Builds are reproducible and isolated from the host.

Decision: the CLI caches API responses in SQLite under ~/.cache with a 24 hour TTL and serves them when the network is down. Today every command calls the API, takes 2 seconds to start, and fails offline. Rejected: an in-memory cache. The title: The tool works offline and starts fast.
